findings.title: sanitizeGroupTitle lets invisible and bidi-control characters through, so a group header can render blank or misrepresent another group
findings.description: sanitizeGroupTitle (src/data/migration.ts:38-44) filters on type only: `typeof value !== 'string'` -> '', then `.trim().slice(0, 40)`. `String.prototype.trim` strips WhiteSpace + LineTerminator, but not Unicode format characters (category Cf) and not C0/C1 control characters. Verified in node: `('\u200B\u202E').trim()` returns the string unchanged, i.e. non-empty. So a hand-edited data.json with `"title": "\u200B"` (zero-width space), `"\uFEFF"`, `"\u3164"` (Hangul filler) or `"\u202E..."` (right-to-left override) survives sanitization and is persisted as a non-empty title. Because '' is the sentinel for "use the default localized name" (types.ts:29), a title made only of invisible characters is not empty, so the default name is suppressed and the group header renders visually blank. A leading U+202E reverses the visible order of the rest of the string, which is the classic way to make one label read as another. Embedded (non-edge) control characters such as `\n`, `\t`, `\u0000` are likewise preserved. This is not XSS: the title reaches the UI through Svelte `{...}` interpolation and `{@html}` is banned project-wide (grep over src/ finds it only inside a comment in src/ui/groupTitle.ts), so the impact is display integrity, not script execution.
findings.impact: A damaged or maliciously crafted data.json (Obsidian vaults are routinely synced through Dropbox/iCloud/git and shared) can produce a board where a group has no readable name at all, or where one group's header visually impersonates another. Since the sanitized value is written straight back to disk by loadPluginData() (src/main.ts:52-59), the state is sticky across restarts.

findings.title: The 40-character cap counts UTF-16 code units, so slice can split a surrogate pair and leave a lone surrogate in data.json
findings.description: `value.trim().slice(0, GROUP_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH)` (src/data/migration.ts:43) truncates by UTF-16 code unit. Verified in node: `('a'.repeat(39) + '\u{1F600}').slice(0, 40)` yields a string ending in the lone high surrogate `\uD83D`. That value is then handed to Obsidian's saveData -> JSON.stringify. Modern engines implement well-formed JSON.stringify (ES2019) and escape the lone surrogate as `\ud83d`, so the file stays parseable and the value round-trips — this is a rendering/data-hygiene defect, not a corruption-on-write one. The same cap also does no grapheme clustering: 40 combining marks (U+0300 stacking, "Zalgo") pass the cap as a legal 40-character title while rendering far taller than one header row.
findings.impact: A title ending on an emoji or any astral-plane character at the boundary is persisted with a broken code point and renders as U+FFFD. A combining-mark title can visually overflow the group header and overlap adjacent board chrome. Both are cosmetic, but both are permanent once written back on the first load.
findings.recommendation: Truncate by code point: `return [...cleaned.trim()].slice(0, GROUP_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH).join('')`. The existing boundary tests (`'c'.repeat(40)` unchanged, `'a'.repeat(41)` capped) still pass; add one case with an astral character straddling the boundary. Bounding combining marks is optional and can stay a known limitation — the CSS side (`overflow: hidden` on the header) is the cheaper mitigation there.

findings.category: A08: Software and Data Integrity Failures
findings.title: Sanitization ignores the stored version, so a file written by a newer plugin version is silently downgraded and rewritten
findings.description: The sanitization block (src/data/migration.ts:152-157) deliberately sits outside every `if (version < N)` branch — correct per Decision 6, and it is what repairs data damaged after migration. But it is also unconditional in the *forward* direction: for `version > 8` the migration blocks are all skipped and the sanitizers still run. sanitizeGroupOrder drops every id not in the current GROUP_IDS and sanitizeGroupTitle truncates at the currently compiled 40. loadPluginData() then writes the result back with `await this.saveData(this.data)` (src/main.ts:52-59) before anything is rendered, with no backup and no user-facing message (also per Decision 6). So opening a v9 data.json with a v8 build is destructive, not read-only: a seventh group id would be dropped from groupOrder, and titles longer than a future, larger cap would be cut. The realistic trigger is not a deliberate downgrade but a vault synced across two machines running different plugin versions, which is the normal state of an Obsidian vault on Sync/Dropbox/git.
findings.impact: Permanent, silent loss of user configuration when a vault is opened by an older plugin build than the one that wrote it. Today the blast radius is zero because no schema above 8 exists and GROUP_IDS is fixed; it becomes real the first time the group set or the title cap changes.
findings.recommendation: Not a defect of this task's scope, and Decision 10 rules out introducing a CURRENT_VERSION constant, so record it rather than fix it here. When schema 9 lands, gate the destructive part on the stored version — e.g. run the sanitizers only when `version <= 8`, or (better) have migrateData return early with the data untouched when it sees a version it does not understand, so an unknown-future file is never rewritten. Worth a line in the decisions log because the tech-spec's Backward Compatibility section only reasons about older data.

findings.title: The sanitization block itself can throw on malformed board/groups shapes, which aborts plugin load — the sanitizers never throw, their caller can
findings.description: The file-level comment (src/data/migration.ts:9-10) promises "Both sanitizers take `unknown` and never throw", which is accurate for the two functions. The unconditional block that calls them is not equally defensive. `for (const board of result.boards) { board.groupOrder = ...; for (const group of Object.values(board.groups)) { group.title = ...; } }` throws TypeError when: `board` is `null` (property assignment on null); `board.groups` is missing, `null`, or a primitive (`Object.values(undefined)` throws); or any own value of `board.groups` is `null` or a primitive — module code is strict mode, so `(42).title = ''` throws rather than silently no-op'ing. migrateData is called from loadPluginData() before the view exists, so the exception rejects onload() and Obsidian reports the plugin as failed to load with no board at all — exactly the outcome the task names as the thing sanitization must prevent. Mitigating context, and the reason this is minor and not major: cleanupCompletedTasks (`board.groups.completed.completedRetentionDays`, src/data/cleanup.ts:4) and cleanupOrphanedTasks (`Object.values(board.groups)` then `group.taskIds.forEach`, src/data/cleanup.ts:22-26) run immediately afterwards in the same function and throw on every one of these same shapes. I checked each case individually — I could not construct an input that the new block kills but the pre-existing cleanup pass would have survived. So this commit moves the failure earlier, it does not create a new class of unloadable file. The block's own comment claim ("iterating the groups that exist rather than GROUP_IDS keeps a board with a missing group from throwing") is correct and is a genuine improvement over the `version < 5` block, which does throw on a missing group id.
findings.impact: None beyond the status quo today. The concern is that the header comment reads as a stronger guarantee than the code provides, so a future reader may assume migrateData is total over arbitrary JSON and skip a guard elsewhere.

findings.title: sanitizeGroupOrder scans the whole stored array with no early exit or input bound
findings.description: `for (const item of value as unknown[])` (src/data/migration.ts:23-28) walks every element of the stored array even though the result can never contain more than six ids and `seen` is full after at most six accepted items. A corrupted or hand-edited `groupOrder` with millions of entries costs O(n) with a 6-element `Array.prototype.includes` scan per item, on the main thread, inside onload, on every single load. The output is correctly bounded, so nothing accumulates on disk — this is CPU only, and the amplification over the JSON.parse that Obsidian already performed on the same bytes is small. Flagging it because it is the one place in the new code where attacker/corruption-controlled length drives loop count, and the fix is one line.
findings.impact: A pathologically large groupOrder array delays plugin load proportionally to its length. Realistically bounded by what JSON.parse already survived, so the practical impact is a slow start, not a hang.
findings.recommendation: Add `if (seen.size === GROUP_IDS.length) break;` at the end of the loop body. Optionally also bound the scan (`value.slice(0, 64)`) so the cost is constant regardless of stored length. Existing tests are unaffected; add a case asserting a long array with a valid prefix returns the prefix order.

findings.title: Unknown keys inside board.groups are neither validated nor pruned — they get a title written and are persisted forever (no prototype pollution, verified)
findings.description: Prototype pollution was the specific concern here, so stating the analysis explicitly: it is clean. The order path gates every stored value through `GROUP_IDS.includes(id)` (src/data/migration.ts:25), which uses SameValueZero with no coercion, so strings like `'__proto__'`, `'constructor'` or `'prototype'` are dropped and can never reach a property write. The title path uses `Object.values(board.groups)`, which reads own enumerable *values* and never writes through a key from stored JSON, so no attacker-controlled string is ever used as an assignment target. I verified that `JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"x":1}}')` materialises `__proto__` as an own enumerable data property (Object.values length 1) — so such an entry *is* visited by the loop, but the write lands on that plain object's own `title`, not on Object.prototype, and `Object.getPrototypeOf` is untouched. The residual, much smaller issue: the loop treats every own value of `board.groups` as a group, so junk keys (`'archive'`, `'__proto__'`, anything) are decorated with `title` and carried through migrateData into the `saveData` at src/main.ts:59, load after load, never pruned. Symmetric with groupOrder, which *does* drop unknown ids — the two fields disagree on what "a group that exists" means.
findings.impact: No prototype pollution and no privilege consequence. Junk group entries survive indefinitely in data.json and slowly inflate it if something keeps adding them; cleanupOrphanedTasks (src/data/cleanup.ts:23) also treats such entries as real groups, so task ids parked under an unknown key keep those tasks alive.
findings.recommendation: Leave as is for this task — pruning unknown group keys is a data-destroying operation that deserves its own decision, and CLAUDE.md forbids widening scope. If it is ever addressed, do it by iterating `GROUP_IDS` for the *write* while keeping the `Object.values` read for tolerance, and delete unknown keys only behind an explicit migration step. Recording the asymmetry (groupOrder drops unknown ids, groups keeps unknown keys) in the decisions log is enough for now.
